To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Holocene gastropod shell layer of the Rhone fan is the result of a strengthening of the Mediterranean deep-sea currents since the end of glacial time.
a thick layer of pteropods (and heteropods) was deposited in a distributive Rhone deep sea channel during the Holocene, whereas the underlying sediment is of Wurmean age.

the pteropod layer in the Rhônes deep-sea fan was deposited during the Holocen, that it is the result of an increased bottom current activity in the distributive channels of this deep sea fan, that it is related to the important climatic and zoogeographic changes that occurred in this region since the end of Würmian times, and that it is an important marker for the Holocen.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following points:
    1. to determine the origin and the significance of a thick layer of pteropods found at the bottom of the Rhone distributive channels
    2. to determine the paleoceanographic significance of the pteropod layer
    3. to study the changes in the sedimentation regime in the Rhone fan and the Rhone canyon during the Holocene

the following points: (1) the origin of the pteropod shell layer, (2) its significance in relation with the Holocene climatic change in the Mediterranean Sea, (3) the significance of this layer in relation with the bottom currents of the deep sea fan, and (4) the significance of the bottom current changes in the deep sea fan in relation to the climatic change in general
the origin, the significance and the paleoecologic implications of a pteropod-rich layer found in the Rhone delta.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this pteropod-rich sedimentary deposit is the product of an important change in sedimentation in a distributive system of the deep sea fan.
this thick deposit is a good example of a sedimentary layer which is related to the climatic changes that occurred at the beginning of the Holocene.

the Holocene pteropod layer represents the first record of a significant change in the sedimentation of the Rhone fan since the last glaciation, which is related to an increase in the intensity of bottom currents in the fan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Holocene sedimentation in the Rhone fan has been strongly controlled by the bottom currents, whereas during the Wurmian times, this sedimentation was mainly controlled by terrigenous input.
this deposit of pterod shells is a good indicator of the Holocene period and that it could be used as a marker horizon.
the Holocene period was characterized by a strengthening of the deep currents in the Rhô ne deep sea fan and in the adjacent deep sea areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Holocene sedimentation in the Rhone fan has been dominated by bottom currents.
the pteropod layer is a very good proxy of the bottom currents and can thus be used to trace paleocurrents and paleoceanography.
the Rhone deep fan is an ideal site to study the sedimentation processes in a deep-sea channel and the influence of bottom currents on the deposition of biogenic particles.
